title: Charge donor recovery damage and successful-replacement time
statement: Let C,W,H,Droot be the exclusive per-encounter correct, wrong, harmless and root-death probabilities, summing to1, with mean encounter time t. After H, competence is destroyed with probability delta in[0,1]; otherwise the same competent initial state returns after additional time tau>=0. For Zterm=C+W+Droot+delta*H>0, eventual correct-root yield is C/Zterm, expected encounters 1/Zterm and mean time to any terminal decision [t+H*(1-delta)*tau]/Zterm. The delay is charged only on successful nonterminal recovery.

requires: Exclusive exhaustive C,W,H,Droot, finite mean t, Zterm>0 and delta in[0,1]; successful replacement returns the same competent shielded start with the same future law.
tau>=0 is additional conditional mean time only after H when recovery succeeds. Immediate terminal damage has no separately supplied delay in this model.

assumptions: Wrong product and destroyed competence are terminal. A harmless encounter is not actually harmless to the parent unless the specified recovery succeeds.
The hS directional claims additionally use the fixed two-register hazards, q,k>0; they do not assert a general speed benefit for delta>0.
costs: Count every encounter and successful recovery time, root loss and donor consumption. Additional disposal/damage time, poisoning, apparatus aging or changed hazards require a different renewal law.
contract.units: C,W,H,Droot,delta,F,Zterm and encounters are dimensionless; t,tau,T use one time unit.
contract.obstruction: Measure recovery damage, conditional recovery time and restoration of the original root/register; retain actual throughput and finite-lifetime obligations.

body: First-step renewal gives F=C+(1-delta)*H*F, N=1+(1-delta)*H*N and T=t+(1-delta)*H*(tau+T). Solve with 1-(1-delta)*H=Zterm. No independence between encounter duration and outcome is needed for these expectation equations, but each successful renewal must have the same future law and tau must be the stated conditional mean recovery time. Substituting the two-register C,W,H,Droot,t from the full note proves two restricted protection benefits at fixed other hazards: for delta>0, decreasing hS increases correct-root yield, since its denominator after multiplication by Z gains delta*hS*DA while numerator q*k is fixed; for delta=0 and tau>0, decreasing hS reduces mean terminal-decision time, whose extra numerator is tau*[hS*DA+q*(hA+e*(1-chi))]. There is no general monotone mean-time improvement when delta>0: early destruction can shorten decision time. Set delta=tau=0 to recover the ideal cancellation. Do not turn an eventual-renewal probability into a capped-retry, finite-lifetime or chemically validated chain certificate. Hypothetical numerical chain rows in the source were not independently replayed.
